title: Pareto's Hidden Second Layer: How 4% Can Drive 64% of Results
alt_title_1: Why Almost Everyone Uses the 80/20 Rule Wrong
alt_title_2: The Fractal 80/20 Math Behind Top 1% Output
description_hook: In 1896, economist Vilfredo Pareto showed that about 20% of people owned about 80% of Italy's land. If that 80/20 pattern repeats inside itself, just 4% of your inputs could drive 64% of your results.

scenes.headline: Nobody Runs the 80/20 Math Twice
scenes.stat_label: OUTPUT GENERATED BY JUST 4% OF ACTIONS
bullets: Everyone quotes 80/20, then stops at layer one
Pareto's distribution is fractal: it nests inside itself
scenes.narration: Everyone knows the eighty-twenty rule, yet almost nobody runs the math a second time. When you do, a hidden second layer appears.

scenes.headline: Vilfredo Pareto's 1896 Land Discovery
scenes.stat_label: 20% OF PEA PODS YIELDED 80% OF PEAS
bullets: He measured land ownership across Italy
The pea-pod garden story is a popular myth
scenes.narration: In 1896, Italian economist Vilfredo Pareto showed that about twenty percent of the people in Italy owned about eighty percent of the land. The popular story about pea pods in his garden is a legend.

scenes.headline: Apply 80/20 to the Top 20% Again
scenes.left_body: 5 tasks out of 25 produce 80% of your weekly progress
scenes.right_body: 20% of 20% = 1 single domino driving 64% of total growth
scenes.narration: Marketing writer Perry Marshall points out that if the pattern holds, Pareto repeats inside itself. Take twenty percent of twenty percent and eighty percent of eighty percent: just four percent of your actions could create sixty-four percent of results.

scenes.headline: Three Passes = 51% From Under 1%
scenes.stat_label: 0.8% OF DECISIONS -> OVER HALF OF LIFETIME RETURNS
scenes.stat_subtext: Eliminate the noisy 96% and protect your 1 vital lever
scenes.narration: Run it one layer deeper and less than one percent of your choices could drive about half of your results. Busy people polish the ninety-six percent; builders guard the one.
scenes.source: Math: 0.2^3 = 0.8% of inputs, 0.8^3 = 51% of results, if the 80/20 pattern holds

scenes.headline: Circle 1 Task Out of Every 25
bullets: Write 25 tasks -> cross out 24 until task #1 is finished
Depth on the vital 4% beats hustle on trivia
scenes.narration: Every Monday, look at twenty-five things competing for your week, circle the top one, and finish it before touching your inbox.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb (advice, not a study)
